biography.plain_text: Dennis M. Jones was a pharmaceutical entrepreneur who founded St Louis-based Jones Medical Industries with his wife, Judith, in 1981. Built around acquiring and marketing established niche medicines, the company became Jones Pharma and went public before its sale to King Pharmaceuticals in 2000. Jones later supported education and employment charities through a family foundation.

long_biography.plain_text:
Jones Pharma built its business by acquiring established medicines that larger drugmakers no longer prioritised. Under Dennis M. Jones, it focused sales effort on specialty products for thyroid disorders, surgical bleeding and anaesthesia. Thrombin-JMI and Levoxyl became central to the portfolio, while successive acquisitions widened the St Louis company's manufacturing and marketing reach.

Jones entered the pharmaceutical industry in 1964 after high school, service in the United States Marine Corps and work in insurance. Sales experience led to an earlier pharmaceutical partnership, giving him the foundation to create Jones Medical Industries. As chairman and chief executive, he combined direct marketing with selective product purchases and disciplined costs. That approach turned overlooked medicines into a substantial public company before his death in 2016.
